Transport and installer verification

Connection recovery, native transports, direct tools, installers and SSH verification procedures.

About 13 min read · 9 sections

On this page

These are version-specific evidence records and procedures, not a claim that every later build was tested. For current installed readiness, run gateway rollout --verify --json. Return to the verification overview.

Active gateway connection recovery

Run the compiled candidate against a verified gateway SDK package:

node scripts/e2e-gateway-reconnect.mjs \
  --package /absolute/release/package \
  --code /absolute/compiled/checkout \
  --root /private/evidence

The check drops only the adapter's shared gateway socket while the real SDK keeps its turn. It requires automatic reconnection without a frontend request, the same SDK process and turn, one genuine terminal event, and recovery of text emitted while disconnected through item/completed. A second case finishes the turn before reconnection. A pending approval case requires the original frontend callback ID, no execution before an explicit fixture approval, and one actual command execution afterward. All inference uses a local mock provider, and all homes and ownership records belong to the fixture. These checks exercise the adapter protocol; they do not prove rendered desktop behavior.

Disconnected native clients (0.6.2)

The signed codex-cli 0.163.0-alpha.10.2 passed scripts/e2e-shared-native.mjs with combined native and gateway ownership over both stdio and the real SDK's Unix proxy. The fixture verifies the exact OpenAI signature, executable, and engine version before accepting the candidate:

node scripts/e2e-shared-native.mjs \
  --gateway /absolute/release/package/dist/cli.js \
  --package /absolute/release/package \
  --candidate-engine 0.163.0-alpha.10.2 \
  --host-capabilities native,gateway \
  --root /private/evidence

Every frontend disconnects while native inference is held. The same host and SDK finish that turn while detached, and a fresh frontend reads its real completed history without another provider request. A separate turn executes one approved command that appends a byte to a fixture counter, then disconnects during its next inference request. After detached completion and resume, the counter still contains one byte and no extra provider request was sent.

Every frontend also disconnects during a pending user approval. Resume replays the original request and settings without answering it or executing its command; an explicit Stop then cancels it and a follow-up completes. Two-client Stop, steering, model and speed isolation, immutable SDK identity, native configuration preservation, and owned-process cleanup also pass. The fixture uses private homes, no copied authentication, and local mock inference. It does not prove rendered desktop controls or the built-in cloud transport.

Staged-adoption regressions separately cover unchanged live plans, primary-daemon activation, legacy-writer deferral, changed plans, signature/runtime failures, post-commit recovery, and exact private receipt checks. Readiness remains pending until staged ownership is active and the host actually holds the native home.

Live adapter upgrade (0.6.1)

Run node scripts/e2e-live-upgrade.mjs --previous /absolute/0.6.0/package --package /absolute/0.6.1/package --code /absolute/compiled/0.6.1 --root /private/evidence. The check copies both complete immutable packages into a private managed layout, starts the released adapter over a private Unix socket, and keeps that one frontend connection open while its 0.6.0 execution host is replaced by the candidate host. A mock provider makes no paid requests.

Before replacement the old host performs a real direct tool command and local Git commit. A deliberately held second turn proves the host's quiet-stop guard refuses a busy upgrade. Once it finishes, the fixture stops only its host, fault-injects removal of its private old package, and starts the candidate host. The already-loaded old adapter must recover its verified SDK through managed/current, resume the same thread with its saved model, provider, workspace and permissions, and use the resumed connection to spawn a child agent that performs a second command and commit. The result independently checks that the original commit was not replayed, the host PID changed, both SDK packages passed receipt verification, native authentication was never copied, and all owned process groups and sockets stopped. It records only sanitized booleans and versions in a live-upgrade-*.json evidence file under the supplied root; active fixture state uses a short private /tmp path so its Unix sockets fit macOS's address limit.

Hostless direct tools (0.6.0)

Run node scripts/e2e-direct-tools.mjs --package /absolute/release/package --code /absolute/compiled/checkout --root /private/evidence. It starts the real packaged gateway SDK through DesktopCatalog, AppServerBackends, and AppServerRouter with no codex-code-mode-host. Two gateway chats carry native rows that respectively declare code_mode_only and no tool mode at all. The selected runtime changes both to explicit direct rows, exposes exec_command (not Code Mode's exec or wait), then uses the SDK's real spawn_agent path to create bare-native child chats. The children edit two isolated workspace files and make local conventional Git commits. The fixture asks for code_mode_only and code_mode_host while only its disposable repository uses full access; the explicit direct rows take precedence. A local mock provider observes successful command-output continuations; the fixture independently verifies exact file bytes, Git history, clean status, completed child turns, saved provider identity, and untouched native config and authentication. It records only sanitized booleans and model/provider identifiers in result.json, copies no authentication, and sends no paid inference requests.

The same script accepts an SDK whose verified receipt pins codex-code-mode-host (0.6.6 and later). Such an SDK keeps native tool modes, so the fixture gives both native rows an explicit direct mode and proves they still win over the caller's code_mode_only and code_mode_host settings. hostlessSdk in result.json records which shape ran. The script also checks that a host sits beside the executable exactly when the receipt names one. The rollout readiness probe runs this script, so every release package with either SDK shape must pass it.

Loaded service release

Run node scripts/e2e-service-release.mjs --package /absolute/release/package to copy public runtime code into an isolated release tree, start its supervisor, move current, and observe a real heartbeat. The supervisor keeps its original runningRelease, and the watchdog detects it even when the injected process inventory incorrectly reports the newly installed release. The check copies no authentication and sends no inference requests.

Catalog generation capacity (0.5.6)

Run node scripts/e2e-generation-capacity.mjs --package /absolute/release/package against a compiled release with its verified gateway SDK. Five real SDK processes load separate catalogs and chats, and each chat remains readable through its original writer. The check then suspends one unloaded fixture SDK, starts a sixth catalog within five seconds, resumes that SDK, and verifies the released sixth generation (which loaded no chat) retires without another acquisition. The SDK may retain the five started chats after unsubscribe; cleanup preserves them. It uses isolated chat storage, copies no authentication, and sends no inference requests. Version 0.5.5 reproduces the four-generation refusal; 0.5.6 passes that part but remains vulnerable to the suspended-engine case. Shared and per-connection adapter regressions also cover retaining loaded chats, active turns, client leases, and reclaiming unused generations. Rendered desktop recovery still requires live activation.

The v0.2.23 source passes the reduced gateway scope checks. The v0.2.22 candidate passed installed Responses terminal checks, and v0.2.21 passed isolated backend ownership and compaction checks. MacBook Pro 2's original Control other devices connection is active through its native relay. Full desktop parity through that connection remains unverified. SSH, Unix proxy, and local engine results do not prove the cloud connection.

Observed transport outage

During the 12 October outage, the primary Mac's inference process remained healthy with no active requests. Its reverse-forward LaunchAgents for MacBook Pro 2 and Studio were unloaded, but not disabled. Tailscale had also stopped. Restoring those jobs and bringing Tailscale up made both remote gateway doctor checks report ready with 25 added models. The earlier Qwen tunnel was restored separately.

The primary Mac's kernel boot time was 5 October. These observations do not show an outage reboot or an automatic-start failure. Why the jobs were unloaded is unknown. Edi reopened the affected original connected-computer model list and confirmed that Claude, Codex 2, Copilot, and Qwen returned without an app restart.

The development code enables a disabled gateway job when the user explicitly registers it, without restarting an already loaded process. Newly owned SSH children use a ten-second connection timeout and one connection attempt before their supervisor retries. The supervisor also supplies these defaults when it starts a child from an older plan; it preserves explicit values and running jobs. These changes are not yet active on the deployed devices.

Device-local inference

On 12 October, the installed v0.2.10 command on MacBook Pro 2 passed an isolated Claude Sonnet 5.5 run using that device's existing subscription login. Its daemon configuration contained only a local Claude provider. It used no inference forward to the primary Mac. The signed SDK streamed replies and reasoning, followed a hidden repository AGENTS.md marker, read and patched a file, retained follow-up history, acknowledged interruption in 3 ms, cleaned up the interrupted request, and completed a recovery turn. Native configuration stayed unchanged, and the isolated Codex home contained no copied authentication.

Device-local Codex 2 GPT-6.1-Sol also passed streaming, hidden repository instructions, file reads and edits, follow-up history, reasoning, interruption, cleanup, and recovery on the test Mac. Its independent gateway registration verified the requested secondary email. Native configuration stayed unchanged, and no primary authentication was copied.

Configurations retaining the 25 public routes are staged on the test Mac and Studio. They are not active. Studio still needs its independent secondary Codex registration. Its Copilot CLI is now installed, authenticated, and advertises all four selected models. Qwen's HTTPS endpoint returned its configured model with authentication. Device credentials and final cutover still need verification before removing the working inference forwards. The existing Codex cloud connection carries chat transport; it does not provision these registrations.

Compaction and silent streams in v0.2.11

The signed Codex SDK passed forced compaction recovery through the updated gateway. An upstream HTTP 400 context-limit error and an SSE context-limit error before the first delta both retained context_length_exceeded in a failed Responses event. With generic stream retries disabled, Codex trimmed history from eight input items to seven, completed compaction, and completed a subsequent turn. The isolated native configuration stayed unchanged and contained no copied authentication. These controlled checks establish the recovery mechanism; the running v0.2.6 daemon has no request failure logs to attribute the reported historical failure to a specific cause.

The signed SDK also passed a controlled silent-stream check with a shortened 500 ms idle timeout. Comment-only heartbeats failed before a 1.5-second reply. Genuine Responses progress events kept the same silent request alive until its real reply completed. Interrupting during that quiet period produced the SDK's actual interrupted status, released gateway capacity, stopped heartbeats, and allowed recovery in the same SDK process. This test used mock inference and an isolated home, with no primary configuration or authentication access.

Installer and local Qwen

The v0.2.0 preflight installer passed repeat installation, a prefix containing spaces and quotes, checksum verification, and protection of an unrelated command. The bundled runtime has no Homebrew library dependencies. The installed command on MacBook Pro 2 registered the added provider at runtime while preserving the native provider default.

Claude Sonnet 5.5, Codex 2 Sol, and local Qwen 3.8 Flash Next passed native agent title reads, renames, live name notifications, and saved-chat resume after a new adapter connection. The isolated native configuration digest was unchanged. This proves the native engine and adapter, not newly rendered sidebar labels.

The installed v0.2.7 adapter also passed ordinary first turns and follow-ups with Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Codex 2 Sol without calling the title helper. Titles set through the app-server naming API stayed unchanged until an explicit agent rename request. Title reads, name notifications, and saved-chat resume still passed. The test used separate native and gateway state directories.

On 11 October 2026, MacBook Pro 2's original connection was migrated to the installed v0.2.7 relay. Its native and desktop login jobs run under one supervisor. The original environment and installation IDs were retained, and the fresh connection returned 36 models. User-driven Claude checks read the image-only code and wrote the exact release-check seed plus CLAUDE_NATIVE_OK on the remote machine. That connection has since upgraded to v0.2.8. The Codex 2 follow-up, saved-chat recovery, and model-list refresh selection still need verification. The user reported that refresh could select native GPT; backend defaults now agree, but that change has not yet passed the matching client UI check.

Qwen runs on the existing DGX Spark vLLM server. Its managed SSH tunnel uses the existing NVIDIA Sync identity without copying the private key. The real Codex loop passed incremental text, random file proof, custom patch and verification, follow-up history, reasoning, interruption (4 ms acknowledgement), worker cleanup, and recovery. The model uses a 500,000-token server context and currently advertises text input only. Native API inference on the isolated test home's primary account was explicitly skipped because that home has no primary login.

The live checks found two translation/startup bugs. Qwen requires system instructions at the beginning, so the chat adapter combines system/developer instructions there while retaining user/tool history order. Credential-free clients could read a saved gateway chat before discovery and create an empty executor. Saved metadata now reads through the native shared store; inference requires an available catalog. Both cases have regressions.

The initial host migration exposed a launchd KeepAlive race and safely refused the upgrade. Disabling the job prevented the short-lived fixture race, but a long-running loaded job could still restart. v0.2.2 asks the owning daemon to unload its own job only after the idle guard accepts the stop. The client then replaces the plist and reenables the job. Failure restores the earlier plist. The real MacBook Pro 2 check waits beyond launchd's throttle interval and passed active-inference and partial-upload protection, idle restart, idle upgrade with the new config, recovery, and the unchanged client token. On 11 October 2026, the installed v0.2.2 runtime also passed abrupt daemon termination: launchd started a replacement process and a new inference request completed without changing the client token. The extended fixture made exactly four calls to the local fixture and removed its temporary service. The working host's previous long-running service also migrated successfully through this protocol.

The daemon and SSH tunnels are per-user LaunchAgents with RunAtLoad and KeepAlive. They start at login and restart after process exit. Remote clients still require the inference host to be awake and reachable; this setup does not provide failover to another inference host.

Desktop SSH transport

On 11 October 2026, the v0.2.3 preflight installer passed the desktop's original app-server proxy transport on MacBook Pro 2. The private Unix socket returned 42 model rows. Claude Opus 5.5 at Max and Codex 2 GPT-6.1-Sol at Ultra passed incremental output, real file reads and patches, automatic repository AGENTS.md loading, image-only code reading, follow-ups, agent titles, interruption, and saved-chat resume through a new proxy connection. Cancellation acknowledgements took 17 ms and 13 ms respectively. Switching the resumed Claude chat to Codex 2 preserved file and image history. The isolated native config digest was unchanged. The test client explicitly resumes saved chats before starting turns after a connection change, as the native engine requires.

The installed v0.2.3 package also passed this full loop on Studio through its permanent SSH inference forward. Claude Opus 5.5 at Max and Codex 2 GPT-6.1-Sol at Ultra passed all 15 checks in an isolated workspace and native home. Interruption acknowledgements took 10 ms and 17 ms. The isolated configuration digest was unchanged during that test. A direct SSH connection to Studio's production adapter returned all 42 catalog entries, including local Qwen. These checks prove the native proxy and backend; the rendered Studio SSH picker remains unverified until the connection is enabled in the client app.

Earlier Studio Control other devices checks reached the native engine directly. The SSH adapter's combined catalog did not establish model availability through that connection. MacBook Pro 2's original connection now uses the installed native relay. Studio still needs that activation and the matching desktop checks. Keep the proven SSH path available until its native replacement passes.

Run scripts/e2e-unix.mjs with the installed gateway and package paths, an isolated native home with public model metadata, a client-only gateway configuration, and a dedicated workspace/image fixture. It starts a temporary Unix listener, runs the native proxy checks, records only results, and stops its owned processes.

A reconnect regression reproduced Node deleting a replacement Unix socket when an older listener closed. The adapter now binds a private socket and exposes an inode-checked hard link. A replaced listener keeps its connected clients until they disconnect, then retires. Tests prove that old clients continue working and closing the old listener leaves the new socket and client usable.

SSH listener startup and proxy lookup use a separate gateway-owned control home. Regressions cover repeated startup, live-listener reuse, recovery after abrupt termination, refusal of an unrecorded path, and preservation of native IPC and configuration. Only the proxy child's home changes; inference keeps the native account home and does not copy its authentication file.

An intermittent CI failure exposed the socket before its ownership record was written. Publication and stale recovery now share a private lock. The adapter writes the record before publishing the socket alias, and simultaneous SSH bootstraps reuse the winning listener. Regressions hold publication at the lock to verify readiness and start two bootstrap processes together.
